speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The first protects recordings and transcripts of flight recorders in accordance with Annex 6 of the Convention on International Civil Aviation or Chicago Convention.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The second increases the penalties for offences pertaining to unauthorised unmanned aircraft operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: And the third enables the National Civil Aviation Security Authority (NCASA) to delegate its powers to any public officer who is not an aviation security inspector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The first set of amendments set out in clause 2 of the Bill will empower the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) to make regulations to protect flight recorder information or any similar information from use and disclosure in line with changes to Annex 6 of the Convention on International Civil Aviation, also known as "the Chicago Convention".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Flight recorders contain critical information, including the pressure-altitude and airspeed of the aircraft during flight, information from other electronic systems on the aircraft, as well as the conversations between the pilots.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Before the latest amendments to Annex 6 of the Chicago Convention, there was no provision on the use and protection of flight recorder information outside the scope of an accident and incident investigation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: These latest amendments were put in place to address the use of flight recorder information in other circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Specifically, recordings may now be used for safety management, such as carrying out safety trend analysis and training, or in carrying out inspections and maintenance of the flight recorder and, when appropriate, for criminal proceedings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: These are the allowable uses in Annex 6 of the Convention on International Civil Aviation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: For example, flight recorder information with appropriate safeguards can be used for analyses of trends as part of an airline's safety management system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Bill will allow CAAS to legislate the circumstances for use of flight recorder information and the appropriate safeguards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Any person with access to the information will be prohibited from disclosing or using the information except in prescribed circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This will enhance confidence that the information, originally intended for accident investigation purposes and which is also useful for aviation safety, would not be misused.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: There will be no limitation on disclosure or use for purposes of accident investigation under the Transport Safety Investigation Bureau Act or for the purpose of reporting a known or suspected act of unlawful interference required by that Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The second and largest set of amendments concern the penalties for offences involving the use of unmanned aircraft.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: CAAS and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) had implemented a regulatory framework to regulate the operation of unmanned aircraft in Singapore in June 2015 following the passing of the Unmanned Aircraft (Public Safety and Security) Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This included a permit regime that adopted a risk-based approach to ensure that operators are responsible and operate unmanned aircraft safely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Since then, the use of unmanned aircraft has risen rapidly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This is a year-on-year increase of 35% and 65% from 2017.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: For the first nine months of this year, CAAS has approved 480 Operator Permits and 2,195 Activity Permits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The purpose of registration is accountability and traceability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We will design the registration process to achieve this objective while keeping it as simple and as convenient as possible for users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: CAAS will be providing more information on the details of this regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Most operators fly their unmanned aircraft responsibly and in compliance with regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Many of these users operate unmanned aircraft for beneficial and innovative purposes, improving work processes and productivity in the areas of inspections, surveillance and aerial photography, amongst others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We are also facilitating trials for more complex uses, such as medical and ship to shore deliveries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Our schools and institutions of higher learning also use unmanned aircraft to teach robotics, programming and other areas in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Unfortunately, there are reckless and irresponsible unmanned aircraft operators who operate in flagrant disregard of the law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: When operated irresponsibly, an unmanned aircraft could endanger others and cause widespread disruption of lawful activities, resulting in significant economic loss.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: One such example would be when an unmanned aircraft disrupts airport operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This has happened to major international airports – Gatwick Airport had about 1,000 flights disrupted in December 2018 while Frankfurt Airport had about 200 flights disrupted in May 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: During the unmanned aircraft intrusions at Changi Airport in June 2019, about 60 flights were affected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This has obviously not served as a deterrent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It is also manifestly inadequate when one takes into account the damage and disruption unmanned aircraft can cause when operated in an irresponsible way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: In particular, we need to make sure that we have higher penalties for repeat offenders who fail to learn from their mistakes and offenders who knowingly or recklessly operate an unmanned aircraft in a manner that endangers lives or property.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Bill, therefore, contains five clauses aimed at raising the penalties for offences involving unmanned aircraft.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Clauses 3 to 7 of the Bill make the following amendments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The maximum fines will remain at $50,000 for first offenders, and $100,000 for repeat offenders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Bill also introduces an enhanced penalty for repeat offenders of a maximum fine of $100,000 or imprisonment of up to five years, or both.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: For the offence of doing any act or causing or permitting an act involving an aircraft, knowing that or reckless as to whether life or property could be endangered, a higher custodial punishment is introduced where this sort of activity involves an unmanned aircraft.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Bill contains examples of what sort of dangerous activity we are looking at.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The challenges of regulating the use of unmanned aircraft in an urban environment are not unique to Singapore and countries around the world are grappling with the same issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The amendments in the Bill are to send a strong deterrent signal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Our Courts will be able to mete out appropriate punishments to errant unmanned aircraft users who endanger aviation and public safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We will continue to proactively finetune the regulatory framework and invest in counter-unmanned aircraft capabilities so as to keep our skies safe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It is to enable NCASA to delegate its powers to a public officer who is not an aviation security inspector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This will give greater flexibility to NCASA to delegate his powers to a bigger group of individuals where the enforcement powers of an aviation security inspector are not required.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Notwithstanding the prescribed circumstances which the Senior Minister of State has taken us through, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether the prohibition against disclosure of flight recorder information, despite the exceptions, will, in any way, allow industry players, interested individuals or parties, or even authorities to rely on this prohibition unfairly and against public interest or safety to prevent disclosure of information whether for fear of prejudicing the respective party's interest or even fear of bad publicity affecting the relevant party.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It brings to mind recent media reports of suppression of disclosure by Boeing staff of concerns relating to the Boeing 737 Max aircraft prior to the two crashes which led eventually to the grounding of the aircraft.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The increase in punishments will, hopefully, deter recreational users from using their unmanned aircraft in prohibited areas and will make the users more aware of keeping their use to allowed areas.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But changing the law per se and charging the odd person and hoping to make him an example may not be sufficient to ensure that all users know the laws.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is important that the Government must be effective in disseminating to the public, especially the drone users, the legal restrictions imposed by the law and the enhancements in punishments.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Sometime last year, I saw a foreigner using a drone at a beach in Sentosa and was later stopped by a security person.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I was not even sure he was arrested or detained.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The person did not seem to know that he was not supposed to use the drone in the vicinity.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In some ways, this is like the problem we see with some people who still do not know that PMDs are not supposed to be used in certain areas.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In an earlier press interview in June this year, Minister Ng also shared that CAAS had asked SAF for professional advice and that SAF has told CAAS, and I quote Minister Ng, "What is out there in the market that they can procure if they want it quickly.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What kind of defences they need, and it's up to CAAS to know what they need." So, it seems that SAF has shared its know-how with the Ministry of Transport (MOT) and CAAS and gave recommendations on the possible technology and equipment which CAAS can consider deploying.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Can he share with this House some details of the work done?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I would also like to ask the Senior Minister of State how confident MOT or CAAS is in avoiding flight disruptions in future should there be similar drone intrusions or attacks, at least the non-weaponised types, if we are to assume that SAF is responsible for all weaponised drone attacks.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If so, can he share the findings with this House?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If not, is the Government confident of finding out who the culprits are?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is this a one-off publicity spin, in which I wonder what is the point of it as we are nowhere near ready for this?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Or is the Government even seriously contemplating use of flying taxis in the near future?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The thought brings some quivers, not because I do not welcome modern technology, but after what we have seen with the introduction of other drones and PMDs and the inability of the law to prevent transgressions or accidents.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: How prepared are we, legally speaking, to handle passenger drones?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We must always try and embrace technological advancements or new applications, but the law must also keep abreast or even stay ahead to regulate technological application and help set the right culture from the onset, instead of playing catch-up.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Dennis Tan has raised a number of questions which I will address in turn.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: On the prohibition of disclosure of flight recorder information, Mr Dennis Tan asked if there is any possibility of abuse by individuals, companies and even authorities, raising the example of Boeing in the United States.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As I have alluded to in my opening speech, there will be no restriction on the disclosure or use of flight recorder information for accident investigation by the Transport Safety Investigation Bureau or for reporting a known or suspected act of unlawful interference.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This is stated in the new paragraph (oa) under subsection 1 to section 3A of ANA.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Practices are in place today to guard against misuse or inappropriate disclosure of flight recorder information.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For example, firstly, access controls to the recorders and the equipment are needed to download or playback the recordings; secondly, an individual who might be recorded in the recordings must be de-identified; thirdly, the information, when provided, has to be in aggregated format; and fourthly, the information has to be transferred by secure means.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Bill will allow CAAS to make regulations on appropriate safeguards for the use and disclosure of recorder information, in line with the provisions in Annex 6.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: On the unauthorised use of unmanned aircraft, Mr Dennis Tan asked about the efforts being made in public education of the restrictions, offences and punishments.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: CAAS works with other Government agencies, including MHA and the Ministry of Defence, to educate the public on how to operate unmanned aircraft responsibly and in compliance with regulations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Apart from issuing advisory flyers that highlight the set of "do's and don’ts" on the safe and responsible operation of unmanned aircraft, CAAS' other outreach efforts include safety series and seminars to engage and educate different user groups on the unmanned aircraft regulatory framework.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As we make enhancements to the unmanned aircraft regulatory framework, CAAS will continue to engage the public to ensure that they are clear about their responsibilities when operating unmanned aircraft and the penalties that they would be subject to for offences involving unmanned aircraft.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will also be working with interest groups to raise awareness of this regulation as well as the stiffer punishments that come with it.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And as for tourists, they will also need to register their drones as well if they want to use unmanned aircraft in Singapore and we will continue to work with CAAS and the Changi Airport Group (CAG) on how to raise awareness on these regulations for tourists.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Dennis Tan also asked for an update on the unmanned aircraft intrusions at Changi Airport in June 2019.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Investigations are currently still ongoing and there are no further developments for me to report at this point in time.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will continue to remain alert for any other unmanned aircraft intrusions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Unmanned aircraft intrusions can be very difficult to detect and counter because unmanned aircrafts can be very small and do not show up well on sensors.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In addition, some perpetrators can site their elusive operations anywhere within quite a large area around an airport because unmanned aircraft are controlled remotely.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: CAAS and CAG, therefore, conduct regular patrols to look out for errant unmanned aircraft operators.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: They are also investing in additional capabilities to better detect and disrupt unmanned aircraft activities and these include the customisation and calibration of commercial systems for Changi Airport with the help of our Defence Science agencies as well as training of personnel to man the systems and respond effectively to minimise disruptions to runway operations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The enhanced penalty framework that I have mentioned just now will, hopefully, serve as a strong deterrent against irresponsible and illegal unmanned aircraft operations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With that, Mr Speaker, I beg to move.
